::: {.lesson-meta}
[Agents]{.pill .t-agents} [Long-Term Agentic Memory · Lesson 4]{.pill .muted}
:::

::: {.tldr}
Episodic memory turns past decisions into **few-shot examples**. Each time an email is triaged, the router searches the store for the **most similar past emails** and shows the model how they were handled. Adding one example changes the agent's behaviour, for that user only, with no code change.
:::

## How it fits

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  E[New email] --> Q{{"search store<br/>(similar emails)"}}
  S[("Store<br/>email_assistant / user_id / examples")] --> Q
  Q -->|"few-shot examples"| T[triage_router]
  T --> D["ignore / notify / respond"]
```

## Key ideas

::: {.concepts}
::: {.concept}
`Example = input + label`

An email together with the right triage decision for it.
:::
::: {.concept}
`Similarity search`

The new email is the query. The store returns the closest past examples.
:::
::: {.concept}
`Per-user namespace`

Examples live under `("email_assistant", user_id, "examples")`, separate from semantic facts (`"collection"`).
:::
::: {.concept}
`Store in a node`

A graph node can receive `config` and `store` as arguments, and read memory before calling the model.
:::
:::

## Saving an example

```python
import uuid

email = {
    "author": "Tom Jones <tom.jones@bar.com>",
    "to": "John Doe <john.doe@company.com>",
    "subject": "Quick question about API documentation",
    "email_thread": "Hi John - want to buy documentation?",
}

store.put(
    ("email_assistant", "lance", "examples"),
    str(uuid.uuid4()),                         # each example gets its own key
    {"email": email, "label": "ignore"},
)
```

## Finding similar examples

```python
results = store.search(
    ("email_assistant", "lance", "examples"),
    query=str(email),     # the email itself is the query
    limit=1,              # the single closest example
)
```

The match doesn't have to be exact. A slightly different email still retrieves this example.

## Formatting examples for the prompt

```python
template = """Email Subject: {subject}
Email From: {from_email}
Email To: {to_email}
Email Content:
{content}
> Triage Result: {result}"""

def format_few_shot_examples(examples):
    blocks = []
    for eg in examples:
        email = eg.value["email"]
        blocks.append(template.format(
            subject=email["subject"], to_email=email["to"], from_email=email["author"],
            content=email["email_thread"][:400], result=eg.value["label"],
        ))
    return "\n\n------------\n\n".join(blocks)
```

The triage system prompt gets a section with these examples and an instruction to pay close attention to them.

## The triage router with episodic memory

```python
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
from langgraph.store.base import BaseStore

def triage_router(state: State, config: RunnableConfig, store: BaseStore) -> Command[Literal["response_agent", "__end__"]]:
    email = state["email_input"]
    namespace = ("email_assistant", config["configurable"]["langgraph_user_id"], "examples")

    examples = store.search(namespace, query=str(email))
    system_prompt = triage_system_prompt.format(
        examples=format_few_shot_examples(examples), **profile, **triage_rules
    )
    ...   # same as before: call llm_router, return a Command
```

LangGraph passes `config` and `store` automatically when the node asks for them.

## What changes in practice

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Tom's email, no examples stored | **respond** (default behaviour) |
| Same email, after storing it as "ignore" for this user | **ignore** |
| A similar email (other wording, other name) | **ignore**: the example generalises |
| Same email, different user id | **respond**: examples are per user |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- Episodic memory = **examples of past decisions**, used as few-shot prompts.
- Retrieval by **similarity** means one example also covers emails that look like it.
- The namespace includes the user id: each user teaches the agent their own preferences.
- Behaviour changes by **adding data**, not by changing code.
- In the course, examples are added by hand. In a real app they'd come from user corrections, written in the **background**.
:::

## Quiz

<details class="quiz">
<summary>What is stored in an episodic example for triage?</summary>
<p>The email and its correct label (ignore, notify or respond).</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Why does a slightly different email still get the "ignore" decision?</summary>
<p>The store searches by meaning (embeddings), so the closest stored example is retrieved even without an exact match.</p>
</details>

<details class="quiz">
<summary>Why does another user still get "respond" for the same email?</summary>
<p>Their namespace has no examples: memories are stored per user id.</p>
</details>
